$comment: Style pack: Mix Media (handmade cork-board scrapbook). Learned from the user's Hi.Boly director's bible (HiBoly_Directors.pdf, the 'Mix Media Guide') and two reference videos (Video-84385, Video-41225: measured for technique only, no people, footage, copy or brand copied). Four pillars only: the cork board (overlay changes per scene), the character as a real photo cut-out with a torn cream paper edge, handwritten text on torn notebook paper, and illustrated vintage stickers. Stop-motion: every element pops in on discrete frames (12 fps steps), never slides or fades. Workflow and judgment: .agents/skills/style-mix-media/SKILL.md. Cut-outs, boards: rcg mix-media.
label: Mix Media (cork-board scrapbook)
use: Diary-like, intimate stories built piece by piece on a cork board: a real photo cut-out with a torn paper edge, handwritten notes on torn notebook paper, vintage illustrated stickers, pins and tape, stop-motion pops. Personal stories, tutorials, relatable trends, product notes.
from: the user's Hi.Boly director's bible + reference videos Video-84385 and Video-41225 (learned, nothing copied)

hand.$note: Caveat Medium (OFL 1.1, Caveat Project Authors; woff2 latin subset from Fontsource 5.2.8, licence fonts/OFL-Caveat.txt): every on-screen word, black ink on paper

hand-bold.$note: Caveat Bold: one emphasised word, never whole lines

print.$note: bundled HyperFrames serif: only the printed matter INSIDE illustrated props (ticket, stamp value, calendar); never a message

captions.$note: One spoken word at a time, handwritten on a small torn white paper slip near the character (the references' caption chip, kept on paper so text never floats).

motion.$note: Stop-motion: discrete sets on a 12 fps grid (2 frames at 24 fps), no tweens. A pop is three frames: a little big and tilted, a little small, rest. Pins and tape land two steps after their paper.

sfx.$note: Made in this workspace (tools/audio/paper_sfx.py, procedural, no third-party rights), measured in library/sfx/manifest.json. Soft and tactile, ASMR-adjacent: one per placed piece, quieter than the voice.
